stories.title: Nasdaq −4% at midday as the chip rout deepens; S&P 500 −2.4%
stories.body: At 12:00 PM ET the S&P 500 was −2.39%, the Nasdaq −3.98% and the Dow −1.22% (24/7 Wall St.); at 11:31 AM the S&P 500 stood at 7,008 and the Nasdaq at 22,789 (Motley Fool). Losses narrowed later: at 12:36 PM Yahoo Finance quoted the Nasdaq −2.18% and the Dow −0.14%. The Nasdaq 100 is near bear-market territory, 20% below its peak (Yahoo Finance).
stories.why: SPY and QQQ's first three completed 1-hour candles all closed below Tuesday's close; the early close Friday leaves only four hourly closes after today.

stories.title: Megacaps slide: Tesla −4.9%, Amazon −4.7%, Alphabet −4.5% at noon
stories.body: At 12:00 PM ET TSLA was −4.93%, AMZN −4.71%, GOOG −4.47% and MSFT −2.64%, while AAPL (−1.36%) and META (−0.65%) held up better (Structure One feed). Consumer discretionary had the steepest sector losses (Motley Fool); after the open, consumer discretionary was −2.8% and communication services −2.2% (24/7 Wall St.).
stories.why: Megacaps cushioned Tuesday's chip selloff but joined it today; hourly closes show whether the 12:36 PM rebound in the indexes reaches them.

stories.title: Chips extend the rout: Micron −12%, AMD −9%, Intel −8.7%
stories.body: At 12:00 PM ET MU was −12.00%, AMD −9.02%, INTC −8.65% and AVGO −5.93% (Structure One feed); at 11:02 AM StockTitan had MU −11.16%, AMD −8.99% and AVGO −6.04%, with Lam Research −11.64%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell more than 6%, with Micron and SanDisk its biggest losers (Yahoo Finance).
stories.why: A third straight wide move keeps chip implied volatility high; completed 1-hour closes show whether selling eases into the holiday.

stories.title: Energy outperforms as crude rises; banks slip
stories.body: Energy outperformed the broader market (Motley Fool). At 12:00 PM ET CVX was +0.64% and XOM −0.01%, while BAC was −1.83% and JPM −1.61% (Structure One feed). January crude was $83.51 (+1.78%) and the 10-year yield 4.82%, down 7 bp (Yahoo Finance).
stories.why: Firmer crude and a lower 10-year yield pull these names in opposite directions; their hourly closes show which input dominates.

stories.title: Nvidia −8% as Huang's return fails to steady the AI trade
stories.body: Nvidia was −8.37% at 11:02 AM ET (StockTitan) and $144.21 (−7.19%) at 12:36 PM (Yahoo Finance), after a $155.38 Tuesday close. Yahoo Finance tied the drop to profitability and overinvestment worries around AI; Huang's reinstatement as CEO on Monday "may have temporarily stabilized" the trade. Trump told the New York Post a Huang pardon is "always an option"; Huang testifies before Congress next week (Yahoo Finance).
stories.why: Political and AI headlines are moving the stock within sessions; completed 1-hour closes filter the intraday noise.

stories.title: Gold −3% to $3,454.60; silver ETF −4.5%
stories.body: Gold tumbled 3.01% to $3,454.60 as of 11:31 AM ET (Motley Fool). At 12:00 PM ET GLD was $317.65 (−2.40%) and SLV $35.17 (−4.53%) (Structure One feed), extending Tuesday's losses.
stories.why: Metals are falling with stocks rather than hedging them; GLD and SLV hourly closes show whether that selling continues.

stories.title: USTR proposes Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies
stories.body: The USTR proposed tariffs on 14 of 16 economies investigated: up to 35% on Vietnam, 25% on India, 20% on China and Singapore, 15% on the EU and up to 15% on Japan, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan; comments are due Jan. 5, 2027, with hearings from Jan. 25 (StockTitan). They would stack on existing tariffs, topping 40% in some areas (Yahoo Finance). Iran said four tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz (Saxo).
stories.why: Trade and shipping headlines can gap prices between sessions; OXY and USO hourly closes show how oil-linked names absorb them.

stories.title: VIX near 30 at midday, up 15%
stories.body: The VIX was 30.38 (+15.19%) on Yahoo Finance's quote bar at midday, after 31.46 before the open. Early Wednesday, Saxo noted December VIX futures at 24.40 with the term structure in backwardation and SKEW at 139.16.
stories.why: A VIX near 30 keeps option premiums high; this week's short-dated options also span Thursday's closure and Friday's early close.

stories.title: 10-year yield falls 7 bp to 4.82% as hike odds hold near 98%
stories.body: The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.82%, down 7 bp, and the 30-year 5.24% (Yahoo Finance). Traders priced about a 98% chance of a 25 bp hike at the Dec. 9 meeting (CME FedWatch via Yahoo Finance). The Beige Book is due at 2:00 PM ET.
stories.why: Falling yields alongside near-certain hike pricing point to growth worries; yield moves can shift index ETFs within one hourly candle.

stories.title: Europe turns lower, DAX −1.35%; KOSPI closed −6.2%
stories.body: At 11:35 AM ET the DAX was −1.35%, FTSE 100 −0.62% and CAC 40 −0.45% (24/7 Wall St.). Saxo had Infineon −9.7% and ASML −5.6% on AI spending and tariff worries, while Sanofi rose 9.8% on a $41 billion deal for Insmed. In Asia the KOSPI closed −6.16% and the Nikkei −2.78% (Trading Economics).
stories.why: Overseas chip suppliers are moving with US chip names, adding to overnight gap risk.

stories.title: Core PCE 3.3% beats; Q3 GDP 4.3%; new home sales at a 701,000 pace
stories.body: October PCE rose 3.8% y/y as forecast; core 3.3% vs 3.2% expected (Yahoo Finance, SSBCrack). Q3 GDP second estimate 4.3% vs 3.4% advance and 3.5% forecast (BEA, XTB). Claims fell to 189,000 vs 200,000 expected (Rallies). October new home sales came in at a 701,000 annual rate (StockTitan).
stories.why: The 8:30 AM data showed up in the opening gap, not inside an hourly candle.

stories.title: Nvidia options: 4.6M contracts Tuesday, led by a $150 put expiring today
stories.body: Longbridge counted 4,633,214 NVDA contracts Tuesday, 55% calls; the top contract was the Nov. 25 $150 put (182,925). NVDA traded at $144.21 at 12:36 PM ET (Yahoo Finance), below that strike.
stories.why: Heavy volume at a strike expiring today, now in the money for puts, can add to swings near it; reported activity, not a signal.

stories.title: Ahead: Beige Book at 2:00 PM; Thanksgiving, then a 1:00 PM Friday close
stories.body: The Fed Beige Book is due at 2:00 PM ET (Gotrade). Markets close Thursday and reopen Friday for a half day (Yahoo Finance). OPEC+ ministers meet Nov. 29 (Saxo), Broadcom reports Dec. 9 (Broadcom IR) and the Fed decides Dec. 9.
stories.why: The holiday means fewer completed hourly candles and gap risk around Thursday and Friday's early close.
